items.title: Figure 30: Identify a different everyday example of each simple machine than those usually given.

answer.html: Lever: a wheelbarrow or a bottle opener. Pulley: a crane hook block or a clothesline. Wheel and axle: a bicycle wheel or a faucet handle. Inclined plane: a loading ramp for a truck. Wedge: a chisel, a nail or a door stop. Screw: a corkscrew, a light-bulb base or a spiral slide.

items.title: Get It? Explain how a simple machine differs from a compound machine, using a hand- cranked pencil sharpener as an example.

answer.html: A simple machine is one of the six basic devices (lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane, wedge, screw). A compound machine combines two or more simple machines so that the resistance force of one becomes the effort force of the next. A hand-cranked pencil sharpener is compound: the crank is a wheel and axle, and it turns a screw-shaped cutter that acts like a wedge. Its MA (or IMA) is the product of the individual MAs (IMAs), and, like any machine, it cannot output more work than is input.

items.title: Get It? Why does a power drill have both a low-speed and a high-speed gear setting?

answer.html: Driving a large screw or boring a thick hole needs a large turning force, so the low-speed setting uses a gear ratio with a large IMA that trades speed for force. Drilling a small hole in thin material needs less force, so the high-speed setting lets the chuck turn quickly. One fixed ratio could not do both well.

items.title: Lesson 4 Check Your Progress Problem 1. Classify each tool and describe how it changes the force: (a) a doorknob, (b) scissors, (c) an axe, (d) a wheelbarrow.

answer.html: (a) Doorknob: wheel and axle (the large-radius knob turns a small-radius spindle), so a small force on the knob's rim gives a larger force at the spindle. (b) Scissors: lever (a pair of levers sharing a pivot; the handles are longer than the blades' contact point from the pivot), which increases the force at the cutting edge. (c) Axe: wedge. The blade is driven a long way into the wood, and it converts a small force over a long distance to a large sideways force over a small distance that splits the wood. (d) Wheelbarrow: lever. The load sits close to the wheel (the pivot) while the handles are far away, so a small lifting force at the handles supports a large load.

items.title: 3D Thinking: Research other technology used to generate electricity from waste (such as landfill gas or waste incineration) and write a brief summary.

question.html: Note: This asks you to research outside sources. Below is a representative sample summary of well- known waste-to-energy technologies (verify with your own sources).

answer.html: Landfill gas capture: methane from decomposing trash is collected through wells and burned in engines to make electricity. Anaerobic digestion: bacteria break down food waste or manure in sealed tanks, producing biogas (mostly methane) that fuels a generator. Waste incineration: trash is burned in a furnace, and the heat boils water to drive a steam turbine. Gasification and pyrolysis: heating waste with little oxygen produces syngas or bio-oil for fuel. Each releases energy that was stored as chemical energy in the waste, with some lost as thermal energy because no machine is 100% efficient.

items.title: Get It? Compare and contrast simple and compound machines

answer.html: Both change the size or direction of a force and cannot output more work than is input. A simple machine is one of the six basic devices (lever, pulley, wheel and axle, inclined plane, wedge, screw). A compound machine combines two or more simple machines so that the resistance force of one becomes the effort force of the next (e.g., a bicycle or scissors), and its MA (or IMA) is the product of the individual MAs (IMAs).

items.title: Get It? Why does a car need multiple gears?

answer.html: Starting from rest (or climbing a hill) needs a large force, so the transmission uses a high gear ratio (large IMA) that trades speed for force. At highway speed less force is needed, so a low ratio lets the engine turn slowly while the wheels turn fast. One fixed ratio could not do both well.

answer.html: (a) Screwdriver: wheel and axle (a large-radius handle turns a small-radius shaft), so a small force on the handle gives a larger force at the tip. (b) Pliers: lever (a pair of levers; the effort arm is longer than the resistance arm), which increases the force at the jaws. (c) Chisel: wedge. Pushing the length along the wood converts a small force over a long distance to a large sideways force over a small distance that splits the wood. (d) Nail puller: lever. The long handle (large effort arm) about the pivot gives a large force on the nail.

items.title: 3D Thinking: research other technology used to generate biofuels and write a brief summary

question.html: Note: This asks you to research outside sources, which was not possible from the book alone. Below is a representative summary of well-known biofuel technologies (verify with your own sources).

answer.html: Ethanol fermentation: yeast ferments sugars from corn or sugarcane into ethanol, blended with gasoline. Biodiesel: vegetable oils, animal fats or used cooking oil are chemically converted (transesterification) into a diesel-like fuel. Cellulosic ethanol: enzymes break down crop waste, wood or grasses into sugars for fermentation. Algae biofuel: algae grown in ponds or tanks produce oils that are converted to fuel. Landfill gas / biogas capture: methane from decomposing waste is collected and burned for electricity. Pyrolysis/gasification: heating biomass with little oxygen produces bio-oil or syngas for fuel. Each stores solar energy captured by photosynthesis as chemical energy.
